subject: Status page transparency upgrades — taxonomy naming + customer-facing commitments
related_links: Confluence: Status page transparency upgrades plan
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jun 18, 2024 at 8:42 AM PT
Subject: Status page transparency upgrades — taxonomy naming + customer-facing commitments
Attachments: StatusPage_Taxonomy_Draft_v3.pdf, Incident_Comms_Templates_v1.docx

Ava — can you take a quick pass on the external language before this gets published in Confluence + the docs PR?

Two things I want to lock:
1) Component taxonomy naming (customer-facing) — avoiding internal jargon.
2) What we’re comfortable committing to publicly re: update cadence + post-incident summaries.

Attached:
- Taxonomy draft v3
- Comms templates v1 (Investigating/Identified/Monitoring/Resolved)

My gut check items:
- “Capacity & Routing” vs “Scheduler” (strong preference to avoid “scheduler”)
- “Dedicated Control Plane” / “Private Control Plane” — does “control plane” read too internal?
- “Model Serving (Hosted)” vs “Serving Runtime” (runtime feels too inside-baseball)

Also: we have “post-incident summary within 3 business days for major incidents” in the template notes. I’m fine with that *if* we keep it scoped (major incidents only) and make clear it’s a summary, not a full postmortem / not disclosing sensitive details.

If you’re aligned, I’ll ask Paula to update PM-913 + Elliot to mirror in docs.

—
Evelyn Hart
Chief Product Officer
Redwood Inference


From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jun 18, 2024 at 10:03 AM PT
Subject: Re: Status page transparency upgrades — taxonomy naming + customer-facing commitments

Quick pass — overall direction is good.

On taxonomy naming:
- +1 avoid “scheduler.” “Capacity & Routing” is customer-comprehensible and maps to what they feel (429s, slow starts, region saturation).
- “Serving Runtime” should not be customer-facing. I’d use “Hosted API — Model Serving” (or just “Model Serving”) and keep “runtime” strictly internal.
- “Control plane” is borderline. Some enterprise folks understand it, but it can sound like “internal plumbing.” If we can rename:
  - “Dedicated Management” (or “Dedicated Provisioning & Management”)
  - “Private Deployment Management”
  You can keep “control plane” in internal mapping docs.

On commitments:
- Update cadence: do not promise fixed intervals like “every 30 minutes” across the board. Phrase as: “we will provide regular updates” + “include a next update time.” The latter is actionable and measurable.
- Post-incident summary: OK with “within 3 business days” for “major incidents,” but define “major” in external terms (e.g., “widespread outage” / “significant degradation”), not Sev labels. Also add “when applicable” for third-party/provider incidents so we don’t box ourselves into disclosures we can’t make.

One more: in the templates, I’d avoid acronyms like “SLO burn” / “Sev1” in customer-facing copy.

-Ava


From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jun 18, 2024 at 11:14 AM PT
Subject: Re: Status page transparency upgrades — taxonomy naming + customer-facing commitments

This is helpful.

Agree on “next update time” as the core commitment vs rigid cadence.

On naming, if we go with:
- Hosted API
  - API Gateway
  - Model Serving (by region)
  - Streaming
  - Embeddings
  - Rerank
  - Capacity & Routing
- Console
- Dedicated Management
- Private Deployment Management

Do you feel “Capacity & Routing” overlaps/confuses with “Model Serving” for customers? (Internally it’s partly the same path, but symptom-wise it’s different.)

Also: for “post-incident summary,” I’m thinking something like:
“We will publish a customer-facing incident summary for significant incidents, typically within 3 business days, including what happened, impact, and what we’re doing to prevent recurrence. Some details may be omitted for security or privacy reasons.”

Too strong?

—Evelyn


From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jun 18, 2024 at 12:02 PM PT
Subject: Re: Status page transparency upgrades — taxonomy naming + customer-facing commitments

Re overlap: I think it’s fine if we define them with examples.

- “Model Serving”: errors/timeouts/latency when requests are accepted and being served.
- “Capacity & Routing”: elevated 429s, queueing, inability to acquire capacity, region-level saturation, failover/routing changes.

The key is to include “what you might see” and “what you can do” in each component description.

Re summary statement: close, but I’d soften two bits:
- Replace “will publish” with “aim to publish” (or “we publish” but keep wiggle room). If you say “will,” it becomes a hard SLA in enterprise reviews.
- Replace “prevent recurrence” with “reduce likelihood and improve detection/mitigation.” “Prevent” is an absolute.

Suggested:
“We aim to publish a customer-facing incident summary for significant incidents, typically within 3 business days. Summaries include a high-level description of impact, timeline, and corrective actions. Some details may be omitted for security, privacy, or third-party constraints.”

That should be defensible.

-Ava


From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jun 18, 2024 at 1:37 PM PT
Subject: Re: Status page transparency upgrades — taxonomy naming + customer-facing commitments

Got it. I’ll adopt your wording.

Next steps on my side:
- Ask Paula to update PM-913 with the naming changes (no “runtime,” no “scheduler,” no “Sev” language in external docs).
- Ask Elliot to mirror the commitments into the docs PR copy.
- Make sure the Confluence page has explicit “examples of partial impact” per component (esp Streaming-only vs API Gateway, and region-specific serving).

One nuance: do we need “API Gateway” as a separate component, or is that too implementation-specific? Some customers do ask “is it auth, is it rate limiting, is it the model?” so I lean yes.

—Evelyn


From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jun 19, 2024 at 11:26 AM PT
Subject: Re: Status page transparency upgrades — taxonomy naming + customer-facing commitments

Agree keep “API Gateway.” Even if it’s implementation-specific, it’s a useful mental model and reduces support churn (“is it auth vs serving”).

If you include it, add a sentence that it covers authentication, request acceptance, and non-model request handling (rate limiting, request validation), and link to customer actions (check API keys, retry with exponential backoff, etc.).

Otherwise aligned. Thanks for pushing this — the enterprise reviews keep coming back to “tell me what’s impacted,” and this makes us sound like adults.

-Ava
